title: Chapter 4 Quiz 12
description: A mix of everything in Chapter 4. Say how sure you are before you check each answer.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: An array is declared [1..8]. How many cells?
questions.explanation: 8 - 1 + 1 = 8. Watch out: the number of cells equals the last index only when the array starts at 1.

questions.question: tab = [4, 9, 2, 7]. What is the average?
questions.explanation: 22 / 4 = 5.5. Watch out: with DIV it would be 5.

questions.question: tab = [6, 1, 9, 4]. What is the position (index) of the maximum?
questions.explanation: The maximum is 9, in cell 3. Watch out: we are asked for the position, not the value.

questions.question: Which structure holds a student's name, age and average together?
questions.explanation: Different types under one name: a record. Watch out: an array holds a single type.

questions.question: Which structure keeps data after the program ends?
questions.explanation: Arrays and variables live in RAM only.

questions.question: Selection sort of [9, 4, 7]. Array after each pass.
questions.explanation: Pass 1 brings 4 to the front; pass 2 swaps 9 and 7. Watch out: the array is sorted after the last swap, not before.

questions.question: Bubble sort of [3, 2, 1]. Array after each pass.
questions.explanation: Pass 1: 2 1 3. Pass 2: 1 2 3. Watch out: after pass 1 only the last cell is final.

questions.question: Delete position 3 of [5, 6, 7, 8]. What value is now in position 3?
questions.explanation: 8 shifts left into position 3. Watch out: the deleted value is 7, and the new array is [5, 6, 8].

questions.question: How many cells does an array [1..4, 1..5] have?
questions.explanation: 4 × 5 = 20. Watch out: the cells are multiplied, not added (9).

questions.question: This should find the minimum of tab[1..5]. One line is wrong. Find it and type the corrected line.
questions.code:
Let min ← 0
For i From 2 To 5 Do
    If tab[i] < min Then
        min ← tab[i]
    EndIf
EndFor
questions.explanation: min must start with the first element. Watch out: with min ← 0, positive values are never smaller, so the answer stays 0.

questions.question: This should read the age of a student record. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
TYPE STUDENT = RECORD
    Name: string
    Age: integer
END RECORD
Declare Student As STUDENT
Read(Student[Age])
questions.explanation: A field is reached with the dot. Watch out: square brackets are for array indexes.

questions.question: The product of an array must start at 0.
questions.explanation: It starts at 1. Watch out: starting at 0 would keep the product at 0.

questions.question: Bubble sort and selection sort are both O(n²).
questions.explanation: Both use two nested loops. Watch out: they are different algorithms with the same complexity.
